texts.preamble: Sita Ram Sharma vs State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 14 December, 2017 Author: Rajesh Shankar Bench: Rajesh Shankar In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi W.P.(C) No.7014 of 2017 with I.A. No.9561 of 2017 ----- Sita Ram Sharma, son of Lt. Ram Kewal Sharma, resident of Dev Nagar, Shiv Mandir Line, Kalimati, P.O. & P.S. Sakchi, Jamshedpur, District East Singhbhum. .......... Petitioner. -Versus- 1. State of Jharkhand. 2. The Deputy Commissioner, Singhbhum East. 3. Superintendent of Police, Singhbhum East. 4. Sub Divisional Magistrate, Dhalbhum (Jamshedpur). 5. Jamshedpur Notified Area Committee, Jamshedpur. .......... Respondents. ------ Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Shankar ------ For the Petitioner: Mr. P.A.S. Pati, Advocate For the State : Mr. Atanu Banerjee, G.A. For Jnac : Mr. Amarendra Kumar, Advocate ------ 02/14.12.2017 :
texts.facts: The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the respondents not to forcibly remove or demolish the shop of the petitioner pursuant to an announcement made in the locality that the shops standing in Sakchi Market Area, Jamshedpur will be demolished. 2. In I.A. No.9561 of 2017, the petitioner has prayed for restraining the respondents from taking any coercive measure to demolish the shop of the petitioner. It is further submitted that in the last week of November, 2017, the respondents visited the shop of the petitioner and asked him to vacate the same failing which the said shop would be demolished. It is, thus, submitted that the respondents may demolish the shop of the petitioner without any formal notice or proceeding and with the aforesaid apprehension the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner runs a betel shop, situated at Daru Bhatti Road, Line No.22, Kasidih Chowk, P.O. & P.S. Sakchi, Jamshedpur, District East Singhbhum. The father of the petitioner had been carrying out the business activity of betel shop since decades and after the demise of his father, the petitioner has been carrying out the said business. Learned counsel further submits that a trade licence was granted by the respondent-Jamshedpur Notified Area Committee in the year 1987 itself and the licence fee for the said betel shop has been paid by the petitioner till the year 2017-18. The petitioner has also been granted a registration certificate under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 on 15th June, 2017, which is valid for a Sita Ram Sharma vs State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 14 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183878625/ 1 period of five years. 4. Learned counsel for the respondent-State and Jamshedpur Notified Area Committee jointly submit that it is not clear from the writ petition that any notice for evicting the petitioner from his place of business has been issued or not.
